numerical_characteristics.magnitude: masked input value 100.0 (large) at a where=False position, which makes the unmasked gradient NaN
category_specific_evidence: PR#25791 example: x=[0.,0.,100.] with where=[True,True,False] gives grad [0.5,0.5,nan] before the fix; the masked entry should be exactly 0 with no NaN.
The PR example input is printed as [0., 0. 100.] (missing comma); the passage intent is evidently [0., 0., 100.].
Passage test testLogSumExpWhereGrad: x=[0.,0.,0.,0.,100.], where=arange(5)<4, expected grad [0.25,0.25,0.25,0.25,0.]; the masked entry must be exactly 0.
Fix in jax/_src/ops/special.py logsumexp: when where is not None, a = jnp.where(where, a, 0) projects masked inputs before computation so gradients at masked positions are 0.
PR notes an alternative fix via custom_jvp was considered but the projection approach was chosen.
Special value handling: NaN arises in the gradient at masked positions from a large masked input; the correct handling is a gradient of exactly 0 at masked positions.
reproduction_risks: Special value involved is NaN in the gradient at masked positions (pre-fix behavior); the passages give no evidence on +/-inf, signed zero, or subnormal handling.

Passages do not state the buggy commit date (PR DATE blank) or any jax version constraint.
Projecting masked inputs to 0 means masked -inf inputs are not discussed in the passages, so their handling is unknown.
The example input typo [0., 0. 100.] must be corrected to [0., 0., 100.] for a faithful reproduction.
